name: Air Fryer
summary: What an air fryer really is, what it does well, and converting oven recipes.

sections.heading: What it is
blocks: An air fryer is a small, powerful convection oven: a heating element and a strong fan blowing hot air around a basket. It doesn't fry; it roasts quickly, and because the space is small, it preheats fast and crisps well with little oil.

sections.heading: What it's good at

items: Frozen foods made for the oven: fries, nuggets, fish sticks.
Chicken wings and thighs with crisp skin.
Roasted vegetables in small batches: Brussels sprouts, broccoli, potatoes.
Reheating fried food and pizza so it's crisp again, not soggy like in the microwave.

blocks: It's not great for wet batters (they drip through the basket), big roasts, or large amounts: a basketful of food steams instead of crisping.

items: Don't overfill the basket: a single layer with gaps, cooking in batches if needed.
Shake the basket or turn food halfway through.
Toss food in a teaspoon or two of oil for browning; skip aerosol cooking sprays, which can damage nonstick baskets.
Check meat with a thermometer: the outside browns fast and can look done before the inside is. See the [doneness chart](guide:doneness-and-food-safety#doneness-chart).

blocks.text: Converting an oven recipe: lower the temperature by about 25°F (15°C) and cut the time by about 20%, then check early. Times vary a lot by model.
